key_insight: Low DFT prediction errors do not guarantee reliable dynamics in disordered carbon; MACE-MH-1 was the most consistently robust foundation potential tested.
engineering_relevance: Foundation potentials can support nanoporous-carbon modelling, but application-specific stability and structural validation are essential before deployment.
method: Screened six foundation MLIPs using DFT energy and force errors plus binding curves.
Tested four models with melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics.
Evaluated structural observables in pure and O/H-containing disordered carbons.
evidence_signal: Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories exposed failures missed by low DFT errors, while all four MD-tested models reproduced principal nanoporous-carbon signatures.
watch_item: Robustness remains application-dependent: OMAT-based models shared structural biases despite differing architectures, highlighting training-coverage concerns.
paper_title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
